```{r helper-functions, include=FALSE}
shufttest<- function(data,shufdata,column){
  t <- c("coef"=NA,"Pvalue"=NA)
  if(nrow(data)<2){return(t)}
  r <- t.test(data[[column]],shufdata)
  t[1] <- r$estimate[[1]]-r$estimate[[2]]
  t[2] <- r$p.value
  return(t)
}

shufttest <- function(data, shufdata, column) {
  t <- c("coef" = NA, "Pvalue" = NA)
  if (nrow(data) < 2) {
    return(t)
  }
  # Perform Welch's t-test
  r <- t.test(data[[column]], shufdata, var.equal = FALSE)
  t[1] <- r$estimate[[1]] - r$estimate[[2]]  # Difference in means
  t[2] <- r$p.value
  
  return(t)
}

create_barcode_correlation_barplot<-function(data_list, names = NULL, 
                                               presplice_name = "Presplice", 
                                               postsplice_name = "Postsplice",
                                               barcode_prefix = "BC_",
                                               output_file = NULL) {
  # Check if required packages are installed
  required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "reshape2", "dplyr")
  for (pkg in required_packages) {
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop(paste("Package", pkg, "is required but not installed. Please install it with install.packages('", pkg, "')"))
    }
  }
  
  # Load required packages
  library(ggplot2)
  library(reshape2)
  library(dplyr)
  
  # Validate input
  if (!is.list(data_list)) {
    stop("Input must be a list of data frames")
  }
  
  if (length(data_list) < 3) {
    stop("Need at least three datasets (presplice, postsplice, and at least one barcode threshold)")
  }
  
  # Assign names if not provided
  if (is.null(names)) {
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  } else if (length(names) != length(data_list)) {
    warning("Number of names doesn't match number of datasets. Using default names.")
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  }
  
  names(data_list) <- names
  
  # Find indices of presplice and postsplice datasets
  presplice_idx <- which(names == presplice_name)
  postsplice_idx <- which(names == postsplice_name)
  
  if (length(presplice_idx) == 0) {
    stop(paste("Presplice dataset '", presplice_name, "' not found in the provided names"))
  }
  
  if (length(postsplice_idx) == 0) {
    stop(paste("Postsplice dataset '", postsplice_name, "' not found in the provided names"))
  }
  
  # Find barcode datasets (those with the barcode prefix)
  barcode_indices <- grep(barcode_prefix, names)
  
  if (length(barcode_indices) == 0) {
    stop(paste("No barcode datasets with prefix '", barcode_prefix, "' found in the provided names"))
  }
  
  # Extract barcode thresholds from dataset names
  barcode_thresholds <- numeric(length(barcode_indices))
  for (i in 1:length(barcode_indices)) {
    # Extract the number after the prefix (e.g., "BC_5" -> 5)
    barcode_name <- names[barcode_indices[i]]
    barcode_thresholds[i] <- as.numeric(gsub(paste0("^", barcode_prefix), "", barcode_name))
  }
  
  # Create a data frame to store correlation values
  correlation_df <- data.frame(
    Threshold = barcode_thresholds,
    Presplice_Pearson = numeric(length(barcode_indices)),
    Presplice_Spearman = numeric(length(barcode_indices)),
    Postsplice_Pearson = numeric(length(barcode_indices)),
    Postsplice_Spearman = numeric(length(barcode_indices))
  )
  
  # Calculate correlations for each barcode threshold
  for (i in 1:length(barcode_indices)) {
    bc_idx <- barcode_indices[i]
    
    # Presplice vs Barcode
    pre_merged <- merge(
      data_list[[presplice_idx]], 
      data_list[[bc_idx]], 
      by = c("Element", "Allele"),
      suffixes = c(".pre", ".bc")
    )
    
    if (nrow(pre_merged) > 1) {
      correlation_df$Presplice_Pearson[i] <- cor(pre_merged$avg_expression.pre, 
                                                 pre_merged$avg_expression.bc, 
                                                 method = "pearson")
      
      correlation_df$Presplice_Spearman[i] <- cor(pre_merged$avg_expression.pre, 
                                                  pre_merged$avg_expression.bc, 
                                                  method = "spearman")
    } else {
      correlation_df$Presplice_Pearson[i] <- NA
      correlation_df$Presplice_Spearman[i] <- NA
    }
    
    # Postsplice vs Barcode
    post_merged <- merge(
      data_list[[postsplice_idx]], 
      data_list[[bc_idx]], 
      by = c("Element", "Allele"),
      suffixes = c(".post", ".bc")
    )
    
    if (nrow(post_merged) > 1) {
      correlation_df$Postsplice_Pearson[i] <- cor(post_merged$avg_expression.post, 
                                                  post_merged$avg_expression.bc, 
                                                  method = "pearson")
      
      correlation_df$Postsplice_Spearman[i] <- cor(post_merged$avg_expression.post, 
                                                   post_merged$avg_expression.bc, 
                                                   method = "spearman")
    } else {
      correlation_df$Postsplice_Pearson[i] <- NA
      correlation_df$Postsplice_Spearman[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  # Order by threshold
  correlation_df <- correlation_df[order(correlation_df$Threshold),]
  
  # Reshape data for plotting
  plot_data <- reshape2::melt(correlation_df, 
                              id.vars = "Threshold", 
                              variable.name = "Correlation_Type",
                              value.name = "Correlation")
  
  # Split the Correlation_Type into Dataset and Method
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    mutate(
      Dataset = ifelse(grepl("Presplice", Correlation_Type), "Presplice", "Postsplice"),
      Method = ifelse(grepl("Pearson", Correlation_Type), "Pearson", "Spearman")
    )
  
  # Create a proper interaction factor with consistent ordering
  plot_data$Group <- factor(paste(plot_data$Dataset, plot_data$Method, sep = " - "),
                            levels = c("Presplice - Pearson", 
                                       "Presplice - Spearman",
                                       "Postsplice - Pearson", 
                                       "Postsplice - Spearman"))
  
  # Find the min/max correlation values to set proper y-axis limits
  min_corr <- min(plot_data$Correlation, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Add some padding below if there are negative values
  if (min_corr < 0) {
    y_min <- min_corr * 1.1  # Add 10% padding below the minimum
  } else {
    y_min <- 0
  }
  
  # Create the bar plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = factor(Threshold), y = Correlation, 
                             fill = Group)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title = "Correlation between Splice Data and Barcode Threshold Datasets",
      x = "Barcode Threshold",
      y = "Correlation Coefficient",
      fill = "Dataset & Method"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Presplice - Pearson" = "#1f77b4", 
                 "Presplice - Spearman" = "#aec7e8",
                 "Postsplice - Pearson" = "#ff7f0e", 
                 "Postsplice - Spearman" = "#ffbb78")
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    ) +
    # Add a horizontal line at y=0 for reference with negative values
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "darkgray") +
    # Adjust y-axis to show negative values if present
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, 1))
  
  # Save plot if requested
  if (!is.null(output_file)) {
    ggsave(output_file, p, width = 10, height = 7)
  }
  
  return(list(
    plot = p,
    data = correlation_df
  ))
}

# Function to count unique barcodes per Element by Allele type and filter by thresholds
filter_with_allele_counts <- function(data, thresholds = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20)) {
  # Get all unique elements
  all_elements <- unique(data$Element)
  
  # Create an empty data frame to store our results
  result_df <- data.frame(
    Element = all_elements,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Get all unique allele types in the data
  allele_types <- unique(data$Allele)
  
  # For each allele type, count unique barcodes per element
  for (allele_val in allele_types) {
    # Create column name for this allele type
    col_name <- paste0("unique_barcodes_", allele_val)
    
    # Initialize the column with zeros
    result_df[[col_name]] <- 0
    
    # Count unique barcodes for each element with this allele
    for (i in 1:nrow(result_df)) {
      elem <- result_df$Element[i]
      
      # Get rows for this element and allele
      subset_rows <- data[data$Element == elem & data$Allele == allele_val, ]
      
      # Count unique barcodes if there are any rows
      if (nrow(subset_rows) > 0) {
        result_df[[col_name]][i] <- length(unique(subset_rows$revcomp_barcode))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Add columns to indicate if the element meets each threshold for each allele
  for (threshold in thresholds) {
    for (allele_val in allele_types) {
      count_col <- paste0("unique_barcodes_", allele_val)
      flag_col <- paste0("over_", threshold, "_", allele_val)
      
      result_df[[flag_col]] <- result_df[[count_col]] >= threshold
    }
  }
  
  # Return the comprehensive table
  return(result_df)
}

# Function to filter data based on minimum unique barcode counts
# Considering Element and Allele together
filter_by_element_allele_counts <- function(data, thresholds = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20)) {
  # Create a data frame to track counts for each Element-Allele combination
  element_allele_counts <- data.frame()
  
  # Get all unique Element-Allele combinations
  combinations <- unique(data[, c("Element", "Allele")])
  
  # Count unique barcodes for each Element-Allele combination
  for (i in 1:nrow(combinations)) {
    elem <- combinations$Element[i]
    allele <- combinations$Allele[i]
    
    # Get rows for this combination
    subset <- data[data$Element == elem & data$Allele == allele, ]
    
    # Count unique barcodes
    unique_count <- length(unique(subset$revcomp_barcode))
    
    # Add to tracking data frame
    element_allele_counts <- rbind(element_allele_counts, 
                                  data.frame(Element = elem,
                                            Allele = allele,
                                            unique_barcode_count = unique_count))
  }
  
  # Prepare result list
  results <- list()
  
  # Add the count information
  results$all_counts <- element_allele_counts
  
  # Filter for each threshold
  for (threshold in thresholds) {
    # Get combinations that meet the threshold
    meets_threshold <- element_allele_counts[element_allele_counts$unique_barcode_count >= threshold, ]
    
    # Create filtered dataset
    filtered_rows <- integer(0)
    
    # Identify rows in original data that match our criteria
    for (i in 1:nrow(meets_threshold)) {
      elem <- meets_threshold$Element[i]
      allele <- meets_threshold$Allele[i]
      
      # Find matching rows in original data
      matching_rows <- which(data$Element == elem & data$Allele == allele)
      filtered_rows <- c(filtered_rows, matching_rows)
    }
    
    # Add filtered dataset to results
    results[[paste0("over_", threshold)]] <- data[filtered_rows, ]
    
    # Add count info for this threshold
    results[[paste0("counts_over_", threshold)]] <- meets_threshold
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Function to calculate both overall average expression and per-replicate average expression
calculate_expression_stats <- function(data) {
  # Check if required columns exist
  required_cols <- c("Element", "Allele", "Expression", "BiolRep", "revcomp_barcode")
  missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% names(data)]
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # Using data.table if available (faster for large datasets)
  if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(data.table)
    
    # Convert to data.table if it's not already
    if (!is.data.table(data)) {
      dt <- as.data.table(data)
    } else {
      dt <- data
    }
    
    # Calculate mean expression by Element and Allele (overall average)
    overall_avg <- dt[, .(avg_expression = mean(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                         sd_expression = sd(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                         n_measurements = .N,
                         n_barcodes = length(unique(revcomp_barcode))), 
                     by = .(Element, Allele)]
    
    # Calculate mean expression by Element, Allele, and BiolRep (per-replicate average)
    per_rep_avg <- dt[, .(avg_expression = mean(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                         sd_expression = sd(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
                         n_measurements = .N,
                         n_barcodes = length(unique(revcomp_barcode))), 
                     by = .(Element, Allele, BiolRep)]
    
    # Return both tables as a list
    return(list(
      overall = overall_avg,
      per_replicate = per_rep_avg
    ))
  } 
  # Using base R approach if data.table is not available
  else {
    # Create unique Element-Allele combinations for overall average
    element_allele_combos <- unique(data[, c("Element", "Allele")])
    
    # Create unique Element-Allele-BiolRep combinations for per-replicate average
    element_allele_rep_combos <- unique(data[, c("Element", "Allele", "BiolRep")])
    
    # Create result data frame for overall average
    overall_result <- data.frame(
      Element = character(0),
      Allele = character(0),
      avg_expression = numeric(0),
      sd_expression = numeric(0),
      n_measurements = integer(0),
      n_barcodes = integer(0)
    )
    
    # Create result data frame for per-replicate average
    per_rep_result <- data.frame(
      Element = character(0),
      Allele = character(0),
      BiolRep = character(0),
      avg_expression = numeric(0),
      sd_expression = numeric(0),
      n_measurements = integer(0),
      n_barcodes = integer(0)
    )
    
    # Calculate overall stats for each Element-Allele combination
    for (i in 1:nrow(element_allele_combos)) {
      elem <- element_allele_combos$Element[i]
      allele <- element_allele_combos$Allele[i]
      
      # Subset data for this Element-Allele combination
      subset_data <- data[data$Element == elem & data$Allele == allele, ]
      
      # Calculate statistics
      avg_exp <- mean(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      sd_exp <- sd(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      n_meas <- nrow(subset_data)
      n_barc <- length(unique(subset_data$revcomp_barcode))
      
      # Add to overall result
      overall_result <- rbind(overall_result, data.frame(
        Element = elem,
        Allele = allele,
        avg_expression = avg_exp,
        sd_expression = sd_exp,
        n_measurements = n_meas,
        n_barcodes = n_barc
      ))
    }
    
    # Calculate per-replicate stats for each Element-Allele-BiolRep combination
    for (i in 1:nrow(element_allele_rep_combos)) {
      elem <- element_allele_rep_combos$Element[i]
      allele <- element_allele_rep_combos$Allele[i]
      rep <- element_allele_rep_combos$BiolRep[i]
      
      # Subset data for this Element-Allele-BiolRep combination
      subset_data <- data[data$Element == elem & 
                         data$Allele == allele & 
                         data$BiolRep == rep, ]
      
      # Calculate statistics
      avg_exp <- mean(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      sd_exp <- sd(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      n_meas <- nrow(subset_data)
      n_barc <- length(unique(subset_data$revcomp_barcode))
      
      # Add to per-replicate result
      per_rep_result <- rbind(per_rep_result, data.frame(
        Element = elem,
        Allele = allele,
        BiolRep = rep,
        avg_expression = avg_exp,
        sd_expression = sd_exp,
        n_measurements = n_meas,
        n_barcodes = n_barc
      ))
    }
    
    # Return both tables as a list
    return(list(
      overall = overall_result,
      per_replicate = per_rep_result
    ))
  }
}

# Function to calculate average expression by Element (across all BiolRep and Allele)
calculate_element_avg_expression <- function(data) {
   # Check if required columns exist
  required_cols <- c("Element", "Allele", "Expression", "BiolRep")
  missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% names(data)]
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # Using data.table if available (faster for large datasets)
  if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(data.table)
    
    # Convert to data.table if it's not already
    if (!is.data.table(data)) {
      dt <- as.data.table(data)
    } else {
      dt <- data
    }
    
    # Calculate mean expression by Element and Allele (across BiolRep)
    element_allele_avg <- dt[, .(
      avg_expression = mean(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_expression = sd(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_measurements = .N,
      n_replicates = length(unique(BiolRep))
    ), by = .(Element, Allele)]
    
    return(element_allele_avg)
  } 
  # Using base R approach if data.table is not available
  else {
    # Get unique Element-Allele combinations
    element_allele_combos <- unique(data[, c("Element", "Allele")])
    
    # Create result data frame
    result <- data.frame(
      Element = character(0),
      Allele = character(0),
      avg_expression = numeric(0),
      sd_expression = numeric(0),
      n_measurements = integer(0),
      n_replicates = integer(0)
    )
    
    # Calculate stats for each Element-Allele combination
    for (i in 1:nrow(element_allele_combos)) {
      elem <- element_allele_combos$Element[i]
      allele <- element_allele_combos$Allele[i]
      
      # Subset data for this Element-Allele combination
      subset_data <- data[data$Element == elem & data$Allele == allele, ]
      
      # Calculate statistics
      avg_exp <- mean(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      sd_exp <- sd(subset_data$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
      n_meas <- nrow(subset_data)
      n_replicates <- length(unique(subset_data$BiolRep))
      
      # Add to result
      result <- rbind(result, data.frame(
        Element = elem,
        Allele = allele,
        avg_expression = avg_exp,
        sd_expression = sd_exp,
        n_measurements = n_meas,
        n_replicates = n_replicates
      ))
    }
    
    return(result)
  }
}

# Function to calculate correlations of expression values across different datasets
calculate_expression_correlations <- function(data_list, names = NULL) {
  # Validate input
  if (!is.list(data_list)) {
    stop("Input must be a list of data frames")
  }
  
  if (length(data_list) < 2) {
    stop("Need at least two datasets to calculate correlations")
  }
  
  # Assign names if not provided
  if (is.null(names)) {
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  } else if (length(names) != length(data_list)) {
    warning("Number of names does not match number of datasets. Using default names.")
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  }
  
  names(data_list) <- names
  
  # Check required columns in each dataset
  for (i in 1:length(data_list)) {
    required_cols <- c("Element", "Allele", "avg_expression")
    missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% names(data_list[[i]])]
    
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop(paste0("Missing required columns in dataset ", 
                  names[i], ": ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  
  # Create result containers
  n_datasets <- length(data_list)
  pearson_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_datasets, ncol = n_datasets)
  spearman_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_datasets, ncol = n_datasets)
  sample_sizes <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_datasets, ncol = n_datasets)
  
  rownames(pearson_matrix) <- names
  colnames(pearson_matrix) <- names
  rownames(spearman_matrix) <- names
  colnames(spearman_matrix) <- names
  rownames(sample_sizes) <- names
  colnames(sample_sizes) <- names
  
  # Calculate correlation for each pair of datasets
  for (i in 1:n_datasets) {
    for (j in 1:n_datasets) {
      if (i == j) {
        # Set diagonal to 1
        pearson_matrix[i, j] <- 1
        spearman_matrix[i, j] <- 1
        sample_sizes[i, j] <- nrow(data_list[[i]])
        next
      }
      
      # Merge datasets on Element and Allele
      merged_data <- merge(
        data_list[[i]], 
        data_list[[j]], 
        by = c("Element", "Allele"),
        suffixes = c(".1", ".2")
      )
      
      # Only calculate if there are matched pairs
      if (nrow(merged_data) > 1) {
        # Calculate Pearson correlation
        pearson_result <- cor.test(
          merged_data$avg_expression.1, 
          merged_data$avg_expression.2, 
          method = "pearson"
        )
        
        # Calculate Spearman correlation
        spearman_result <- cor.test(
          merged_data$avg_expression.1, 
          merged_data$avg_expression.2, 
          method = "spearman"
        )
        
        # Store results
        pearson_matrix[i, j] <- pearson_result$estimate
        spearman_matrix[i, j] <- spearman_result$estimate
        sample_sizes[i, j] <- nrow(merged_data)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create a summary dataframe
  summary_df <- data.frame(
    Dataset1 = character(),
    Dataset2 = character(),
    Pearson_r = numeric(),
    Pearson_pvalue = numeric(),
    Spearman_rho = numeric(),
    Spearman_pvalue = numeric(),
    Shared_elements = integer(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Fill the summary dataframe
  for (i in 1:(n_datasets-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):n_datasets) {
      # Merge datasets on Element and Allele
      merged_data <- merge(
        data_list[[i]], 
        data_list[[j]], 
        by = c("Element", "Allele"),
        suffixes = c(".1", ".2")
      )
      
      # Only calculate if there are matched pairs
      if (nrow(merged_data) > 1) {
        # Calculate Pearson correlation with p-value
        pearson_result <- cor.test(
          merged_data$avg_expression.1, 
          merged_data$avg_expression.2, 
          method = "pearson"
        )
        
        # Calculate Spearman correlation with p-value
        spearman_result <- cor.test(
          merged_data$avg_expression.1, 
          merged_data$avg_expression.2, 
          method = "spearman"
        )
        
        # Add to summary
        summary_df <- rbind(summary_df, data.frame(
          Dataset1 = names[i],
          Dataset2 = names[j],
          Pearson_r = pearson_result$estimate,
          Pearson_pvalue = pearson_result$p.value,
          Spearman_rho = spearman_result$estimate,
          Spearman_pvalue = spearman_result$p.value,
          Shared_elements = nrow(merged_data),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        ))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Return results as a list
  return(list(
    pearson_matrix = pearson_matrix,
    spearman_matrix = spearman_matrix,
    sample_sizes = sample_sizes,
    summary = summary_df
  ))
}

# Function to create expression correlation scatterplots
create_expression_correlation_plots <- function(data_list, names = NULL, 
                                               focus_datasets = c("Presplice", "Postsplice"),
                                               output_dir = NULL, save_plots = FALSE) {
  # Validate input
  if (!is.list(data_list)) {
    stop("Input must be a list of data frames")
  }
  
  if (length(data_list) < 2) {
    stop("Need at least two datasets to plot correlations")
  }
  
  # Check if required packages are installed
  required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "gridExtra", "ggpubr")
  for (pkg in required_packages) {
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop(paste("Package", pkg, "is required but not installed. Please install it using install.packages('", pkg, "')"))
    }
  }
  
  # Load required packages
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gridExtra)
  library(ggpubr)
  
  # Assign names if not provided
  if (is.null(names)) {
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  } else if (length(names) != length(data_list)) {
    warning("Number of names does not match number of datasets. Using default names.")
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  }
  
  names(data_list) <- names
  
  # Check required columns in each dataset
  for (i in 1:length(data_list)) {
    required_cols <- c("Element", "Allele", "avg_expression")
    missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% names(data_list[[i]])]
    
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop(paste0("Missing required columns in dataset ", 
                  names[i], ": ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  
  # Get indices of focus datasets
  focus_indices <- which(names %in% focus_datasets)
  if (length(focus_indices) == 0) {
    warning("None of the focus datasets were found. Plotting all pairwise comparisons.")
    focus_indices <- 1:2 # Default to first two datasets
  }
  
  # Initialize list to store plots
  plot_list <- list()
  plot_count <- 1
  
  # Function to create a single scatterplot
  create_scatterplot <- function(data1, data2, name1, name2) {
    # Merge datasets on Element and Allele
    merged_data <- merge(
      data1, 
      data2, 
      by = c("Element", "Allele"),
      suffixes = c(".1", ".2")
    )
    
    # Only create plot if there are matched pairs
    if (nrow(merged_data) <= 1) {
      warning(paste("Not enough matched Element-Allele pairs between", name1, "and", name2))
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Calculate correlations
    pearson_cor <- cor.test(merged_data$avg_expression.1, merged_data$avg_expression.2, method = "pearson")
    spearman_cor <- cor.test(merged_data$avg_expression.1, merged_data$avg_expression.2, method = "spearman")
    
    # Create annotation text with correlations
    annotation <- paste(
      paste("Pearson r =", round(pearson_cor$estimate, 3)),
      paste("p-value =", format(pearson_cor$p.value, digits = 3)),
      paste("Spearman ρ =", round(spearman_cor$estimate, 3)),
      paste("p-value =", format(spearman_cor$p.value, digits = 3)),
      paste("n =", nrow(merged_data)),
      sep = "\n"
    )
    
    # Get min and max for both axes to make a square plot area
    min_val <- min(c(merged_data$avg_expression.1, merged_data$avg_expression.2), na.rm = TRUE)
    max_val <- max(c(merged_data$avg_expression.1, merged_data$avg_expression.2), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Add some padding
    range_val <- max_val - min_val
    min_val <- min_val - 0.05 * range_val
    max_val <- max_val + 0.05 * range_val
    
    # Create scatterplot
    p <- ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_expression.1, y = avg_expression.2)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
      labs(
        title = paste(name1, "vs", name2),
        x = paste(name1, "Expression"),
        y = paste(name2, "Expression")
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
      ) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(min_val, max_val), ylim = c(min_val, max_val)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
      annotate("text", x = min_val + 0.1 * range_val, y = max_val - 0.1 * range_val, 
               label = annotation, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3)
    
    return(p)
  }
  
  # Create plots for focus datasets compared to all others
  for (i in focus_indices) {
    for (j in 1:length(data_list)) {
      if (i != j) {
        plot <- create_scatterplot(
          data_list[[i]], 
          data_list[[j]], 
          names[i], 
          names[j]
        )
        
        if (!is.null(plot)) {
          plot_list[[plot_count]] <- plot
          plot_count <- plot_count + 1
          
          # Save individual plot if requested
          if (save_plots && !is.null(output_dir)) {
            dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
            filename <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(names[i], "_vs_", names[j], ".pdf"))
            ggsave(filename, plot, width = 7, height = 7)
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create a special plot comparing the two focus datasets
  if (length(focus_indices) >= 2) {
    i <- focus_indices[1]
    j <- focus_indices[2]
    plot <- create_scatterplot(
      data_list[[i]], 
      data_list[[j]], 
      names[i], 
      names[j]
    )
    
    if (!is.null(plot)) {
      plot_list[[plot_count]] <- plot
      plot_count <- plot_count + 1
      
      # Save individual plot if requested
      if (save_plots && !is.null(output_dir)) {
        dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
        filename <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(names[i], "_vs_", names[j], ".pdf"))
        ggsave(filename, plot, width = 7, height = 7)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create a multi-panel figure with all plots
  if (length(plot_list) > 0) {
    # Determine grid dimensions
    n_plots <- length(plot_list)
    n_cols <- min(3, n_plots)
    n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)
    
    # Arrange plots in a grid
    multi_plot <- gridExtra::grid.arrange(
      grobs = plot_list,
      ncol = n_cols,
      nrow = n_rows
    )
    
    # Save combined plot if requested
    if (save_plots && !is.null(output_dir)) {
      dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
      filename <- file.path(output_dir, "all_correlation_plots.pdf")
      ggsave(filename, multi_plot, width = n_cols * 6, height = n_rows * 6)
    }
    
    return(list(
      individual_plots = plot_list,
      combined_plot = multi_plot
    ))
  } else {
    warning("No valid plots could be created.")
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# Function to create scatterplots comparing Alt vs Ref expression values
create_alt_ref_scatterplots <- function(data_list, names = NULL, 
                                       alt_name = "alt", ref_name = "ref",
                                       output_dir = NULL, save_plots = FALSE) {
  # Check if required packages are installed
  required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "gridExtra", "dplyr")
  for (pkg in required_packages) {
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop(paste("Package", pkg, "is required but not installed. Please install it with install.packages('", pkg, "')"))
    }
  }
  
  # Load required packages
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gridExtra)
  library(dplyr)
  
  # Validate input
  if (!is.list(data_list)) {
    stop("Input must be a list of data frames")
  }
  
  if (length(data_list) < 1) {
    stop("Need at least one dataset to create plots")
  }
  
  # Assign names if not provided
  if (is.null(names)) {
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  } else if (length(names) != length(data_list)) {
    warning("Number of names doesn't match number of datasets. Using default names.")
    names <- paste0("dataset_", 1:length(data_list))
  }
  
  names(data_list) <- names
  
  # Initialize list to store plots and results
  plot_list <- list()
  correlation_results <- data.frame(
    Dataset = character(),
    Pearson_r = numeric(),
    Pearson_pvalue = numeric(),
    Spearman_rho = numeric(),
    Spearman_pvalue = numeric(),
    n_elements = integer(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Function to create a single Alt vs Ref scatterplot
  create_alt_ref_plot <- function(data, dataset_name) {
    # First reshape the data to wide format to get Alt and Ref side by side
    # Filter to get only Alt and Ref alleles
    if (!"Allele" %in% names(data)) {
      stop(paste("Dataset", dataset_name, "doesn't have an 'Allele' column"))
    }
    
    if (!"Element" %in% names(data)) {
      stop(paste("Dataset", dataset_name, "doesn't have an 'Element' column"))
    }
    
    if (!"avg_expression" %in% names(data)) {
      stop(paste("Dataset", dataset_name, "doesn't have an 'avg_expression' column"))
    }
    
    # Filter for only Alt and Ref alleles
    filtered_data <- data[data$Allele %in% c(alt_name, ref_name), ]
    
    # Check if we have both Alt and Ref alleles
    if (!all(c(alt_name, ref_name) %in% unique(filtered_data$Allele))) {
      warning(paste("Dataset", dataset_name, "doesn't have both", 
                    alt_name, "and", ref_name, "alleles"))
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Reshape to wide format - handling both data.frame and data.table
    if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE) && is.data.table(filtered_data)) {
      # For data.table, first convert to data.frame for reshape
      filtered_df <- as.data.frame(filtered_data)
      wide_data <- reshape(filtered_df, 
                           idvar = "Element",
                           timevar = "Allele",
                           direction = "wide",
                           drop = setdiff(names(filtered_df), c("Element", "Allele", "avg_expression")))
      # Convert back to data.table if needed
      wide_data <- as.data.table(wide_data)
    } else {
      # For regular data.frame
      cols_to_drop <- intersect(names(filtered_data), 
                               c("n_measurements", "sd_expression", "n_replicates", "n_barcodes"))
      
      wide_data <- reshape(filtered_data, 
                           idvar = "Element",
                           timevar = "Allele",
                           direction = "wide",
                           drop = cols_to_drop)
    }
    
    # Rename columns for clarity
    names(wide_data) <- gsub("avg_expression.", "", names(wide_data))
    
    # Only keep rows where both Alt and Ref have values
    # Handle data.table or data.frame differently
    if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE) && is.data.table(wide_data)) {
      # For data.table objects
      cols_to_check <- c(alt_name, ref_name)
      complete_data <- wide_data[complete.cases(as.data.frame(wide_data)[, cols_to_check, drop = FALSE]), ]
    } else {
      # For data.frame objects
      complete_data <- wide_data[complete.cases(wide_data[, c(alt_name, ref_name)]), ]
    }
    
    # Calculate correlations
    pearson_cor <- cor.test(complete_data[[alt_name]], complete_data[[ref_name]], method = "pearson")
    spearman_cor <- cor.test(complete_data[[alt_name]], complete_data[[ref_name]], method = "spearman")
    
    # Store correlation results
    cor_result <- data.frame(
      Dataset = dataset_name,
      Pearson_r = pearson_cor$estimate,
      Pearson_pvalue = pearson_cor$p.value,
      Spearman_rho = spearman_cor$estimate,
      Spearman_pvalue = spearman_cor$p.value,
      n_elements = nrow(complete_data),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Create annotation text with correlations
    annotation <- paste(
      paste("Pearson r =", round(pearson_cor$estimate, 3)),
      paste("p-value =", format(pearson_cor$p.value, digits = 3)),
      paste("Spearman ρ =", round(spearman_cor$estimate, 3)),
      paste("p-value =", format(spearman_cor$p.value, digits = 3)),
      paste("n =", nrow(complete_data)),
      sep = "\n"
    )
    
    # Get min and max for both axes to make a square plot area
    min_val <- min(c(complete_data[[alt_name]], complete_data[[ref_name]]), na.rm = TRUE)
    max_val <- max(c(complete_data[[alt_name]], complete_data[[ref_name]]), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Add some padding
    range_val <- max_val - min_val
    min_val <- min_val - 0.05 * range_val
    max_val <- max_val + 0.05 * range_val
    
    # Create scatterplot
    p <- ggplot(complete_data, aes_string(x = alt_name, y = ref_name)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
      labs(
        title = paste(dataset_name, ":", alt_name, "vs", ref_name, "Expression"),
        x = paste(alt_name, "Expression"),
        y = paste(ref_name, "Expression")
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
      ) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(min_val, max_val), ylim = c(min_val, max_val)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
      annotate("text", x = min_val + 0.1 * range_val, y = max_val - 0.1 * range_val, 
               label = annotation, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3)
    
    return(list(plot = p, correlation = cor_result))
  }
  
  # Create plots for each dataset
  for (i in 1:length(data_list)) {
    result <- create_alt_ref_plot(data_list[[i]], names[i])
    
    if (!is.null(result)) {
      plot_list[[names[i]]] <- result$plot
      correlation_results <- rbind(correlation_results, result$correlation)
      
      # Save individual plot if requested
      if (save_plots && !is.null(output_dir)) {
        dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
        filename <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(names[i], "_alt_vs_ref.pdf"))
        ggsave(filename, result$plot, width = 7, height = 7)
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create a multi-panel figure with all plots
  if (length(plot_list) > 0) {
    # Determine grid dimensions
    n_plots <- length(plot_list)
    n_cols <- min(3, n_plots)
    n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)
    
    # Arrange plots in a grid
    multi_plot <- gridExtra::grid.arrange(
      grobs = plot_list,
      ncol = n_cols,
      nrow = n_rows
    )
    
    # Save combined plot if requested
    if (save_plots && !is.null(output_dir)) {
      dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
      filename <- file.path(output_dir, "all_alt_vs_ref_plots.pdf")
      ggsave(filename, multi_plot, width = n_cols * 6, height = n_rows * 6)
    }
    
    return(list(
      individual_plots = plot_list,
      combined_plot = multi_plot,
      correlations = correlation_results
    ))
  } else {
    warning("No valid plots could be created.")
    return(list(correlations = correlation_results))
  }
}

# Function to process data tables and identify significant elements based on direction and thresholds
process_tables <- function(data_list, fdr_threshold = 0.1, 
                           pos_fold_change = log2(1.25), 
                           neg_fold_change = log2(0.75)) {
  # Initialize result list
  result_list <- list()
  
  for (name in names(data_list)) {
    dt <- data_list[[name]]
    
    # Detect which fold change column to use
    fold_col <- if ("coef" %in% names(dt)) {
      "coef"
    } else if ("logFC" %in% names(dt)) {
      "logFC"
    } else {
      stop(paste("Neither 'coef' nor 'logFC' found in", name))
    }
    
    # Extract significant positive and negative elements
    pos_sig <- dt[get(fold_col) > pos_fold_change & fdr < fdr_threshold, unique(Element)]
    neg_sig <- dt[get(fold_col) < neg_fold_change & fdr < fdr_threshold, unique(Element)]
    
    # Store results
    result_list[[paste0(name, "_pos")]] <- pos_sig
    result_list[[paste0(name, "_neg")]] <- neg_sig
    
    # Print summary
    cat("\nSignificant elements in", name, ":\n")
    cat("  Positive (", fold_col, ">", pos_fold_change, "& FDR <", fdr_threshold, "):", length(pos_sig), "elements\n")
    cat("  Negative (", fold_col, "<", neg_fold_change, "& FDR <", fdr_threshold, "):", length(neg_sig), "elements\n")
    cat("  Total significant:", length(c(pos_sig, neg_sig)), "elements\n")
  }
  
  return(result_list)
}

# Function to create a Venn diagram exactly as specified
# - Center: elements significant in BOTH datasets with SAME DIRECTION
# - Each side: elements significant in ONLY ONE dataset
# - Excluded: elements significant in both but with OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS or not significant in either
create_direction_venn <- function(processed_data, table1, table2, output_file = NULL) {
  # Get sets for the two tables
  table1_pos <- processed_data[[paste0(table1, "_pos")]]
  table1_neg <- processed_data[[paste0(table1, "_neg")]]
  table2_pos <- processed_data[[paste0(table2, "_pos")]]
  table2_neg <- processed_data[[paste0(table2, "_neg")]]
  
  # Get all significant elements in each table
  table1_sig <- c(table1_pos, table1_neg)
  table2_sig <- c(table2_pos, table2_neg)
  
  # 1. Elements in center: significant in both tables with same direction
  both_pos <- intersect(table1_pos, table2_pos)  # both positive
  both_neg <- intersect(table1_neg, table2_neg)  # both negative
  center_elements <- c(both_pos, both_neg)
  
  # 2. Elements with opposite directions (significant in both, but opposite signs)
  # These will be EXCLUDED from the Venn diagram
  opposite_dir <- c(
    intersect(table1_pos, table2_neg),
    intersect(table1_neg, table2_pos)
  )
  
  # 3. Elements unique to table1 (significant ONLY in table1)
  table1_unique <- setdiff(table1_sig, table2_sig)
  
  # 4. Elements unique to table2 (significant ONLY in table2)
  table2_unique <- setdiff(table2_sig, table1_sig)
  
  # Print summary
  cat("\nVenn diagram for", table1, "vs", table2, ":\n")
  cat("  Both positive:", length(both_pos), "elements\n")
  cat("  Both negative:", length(both_neg), "elements\n")
  cat("  Same direction (center of Venn):", length(center_elements), "elements\n")
  cat("  Opposite directions (excluded):", length(opposite_dir), "elements\n")
  cat("  Significant only in", table1, ":", length(table1_unique), "elements\n")
  cat("  Significant only in", table2, ":", length(table2_unique), "elements\n")
  
  # Create Venn diagram showing only elements with same direction in center
  # and elements unique to each dataset
  if (!is.null(output_file)) {
    # Calculate areas for the Venn diagram
    area1 <- length(table1_unique) + length(center_elements)  # unique to table1 + center
    area2 <- length(table2_unique) + length(center_elements)  # unique to table2 + center
    cross_area <- length(center_elements)  # only elements with same direction
    
    # Create the Venn diagram
    venn_title <- paste("Significant Elements in", table1, "vs", table2)
    direction_venn <- draw.pairwise.venn(
      area1 = area1,
      area2 = area2,
      cross.area = cross_area,
      category = c(table1, table2),
      fill = c("skyblue", "pink"),
      alpha = 0.5,
      cat.pos = c(0, 0),
      cat.dist = c(0.025, 0.025),
      cat.cex = 1.2,
      cex = 1.2,
      fontfamily = "sans",
      cat.fontfamily = "sans",
      euler.d = TRUE,
      scaled = TRUE,
      main = venn_title,
      main.cex = 1.3
    )
    
    # Save the diagram
    pdf(output_file, width = 10, height = 10)
    grid.draw(direction_venn)
    dev.off()
    
    # Create a detailed text summary file
    summary_file <- gsub(".pdf$", "_summary.txt", output_file)
    sink(summary_file)
    cat(paste("Venn diagram for", table1, "vs", table2), "\n\n")
    cat("INCLUSION CRITERIA:\n")
    cat("- POSITIVE: coef > log2(1.25) & FDR < 0.1\n")
    cat("- NEGATIVE: coef < log2(0.75) & FDR < 0.1\n")
    cat("- CENTER: Elements significant in BOTH datasets with SAME DIRECTION (both + or both -)\n")
    cat("- LEFT/RIGHT: Elements significant in ONLY ONE dataset\n")
    cat("- EXCLUDED: Elements significant in both but with OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS or not significant in either\n\n")
    
    cat("COUNTS:\n")
    cat(paste("Both positive (center):", length(both_pos), "elements"), "\n")
    cat(paste("Both negative (center):", length(both_neg), "elements"), "\n")
    cat(paste("Same direction total (center):", length(center_elements), "elements"), "\n")
    cat(paste("Opposite directions (excluded):", length(opposite_dir), "elements"), "\n")
    cat(paste("Significant only in", table1, ":", length(table1_unique), "elements"), "\n")
    cat(paste("Significant only in", table2, ":", length(table2_unique), "elements"), "\n\n")
    
    cat("SAMPLE ELEMENTS:\n")
    cat(paste("Both positive:", paste(head(both_pos, 10), collapse = ", ")), "\n")
    cat(paste("Both negative:", paste(head(both_neg, 10), collapse = ", ")), "\n")
    cat(paste("Opposite directions (excluded):", paste(head(opposite_dir, 10), collapse = ", ")), "\n")
    cat(paste("Significant only in", table1, ":", paste(head(table1_unique, 10), collapse = ", ")), "\n")
    cat(paste("Significant only in", table2, ":", paste(head(table2_unique, 10), collapse = ", ")), "\n")
    sink()
  }
  
  # Return the sets for further analysis
  return(list(
    both_pos = both_pos,
    both_neg = both_neg,
    center_elements = center_elements,
    opposite_dir = opposite_dir,
    table1_unique = table1_unique,
    table2_unique = table2_unique
  ))
}

# Function to create separate Venn diagrams for positive and negative elements
create_detailed_direction_venn <- function(processed_data, table1, table2, output_file = NULL) {
  # Get sets for the two tables
  table1_pos <- processed_data[[paste0(table1, "_pos")]]
  table1_neg <- processed_data[[paste0(table1, "_neg")]]
  table2_pos <- processed_data[[paste0(table2, "_pos")]]
  table2_neg <- processed_data[[paste0(table2, "_neg")]]
  
  # Create separate Venn diagrams for positive and negative elements
  if (!is.null(output_file)) {
    # Create two separate Venn diagrams: one for positive coefficients, one for negative
    
    # 1. Positive coefficients diagram - shows elements significant and positive in either dataset
    pos_title <- paste("Significant positive elements:", table1, "vs", table2)
    
    # Calculate areas - now showing only significant positive elements
    pos_in_table1_only <- setdiff(table1_pos, table2_pos)
    pos_in_table2_only <- setdiff(table2_pos, table1_pos)
    pos_in_both <- intersect(table1_pos, table2_pos)
    
    pos_venn <- draw.pairwise.venn(
      area1 = length(table1_pos),
      area2 = length(table2_pos),
      cross.area = length(pos_in_both),
      category = c(paste0(table1, " (+)"), paste0(table2, " (+)")),
      fill = c("forestgreen", "skyblue"),
      main = pos_title,
      main.cex = 1.2,
      alpha = 0.5,
      cat.cex = 1.2,
      cex = 1.2,
      fontfamily = "sans",
      cat.fontfamily = "sans",
      euler.d = TRUE,
      scaled = TRUE
    )
    
    # 2. Negative coefficients diagram - shows elements significant and negative in either dataset
    neg_title <- paste("Significant negative elements:", table1, "vs", table2)
    
    # Calculate areas - now showing only significant negative elements
    neg_in_table1_only <- setdiff(table1_neg, table2_neg)
    neg_in_table2_only <- setdiff(table2_neg, table1_neg)
    neg_in_both <- intersect(table1_neg, table2_neg)
    
    neg_venn <- draw.pairwise.venn(
      area1 = length(table1_neg),
      area2 = length(table2_neg),
      cross.area = length(neg_in_both),
      category = c(paste0(table1, " (-)"), paste0(table2, " (-)")),
      fill = c("tomato", "gold"),
      main = neg_title,
      main.cex = 1.2,
      alpha = 0.5,
      cat.cex = 1.2,
      cex = 1.2,
      fontfamily = "sans",
      cat.fontfamily = "sans",
      euler.d = TRUE,
      scaled = TRUE
    )
    
    # Save both plots to the same PDF
    pdf(output_file, width = 10, height = 10)
    # Create a 1x2 layout for the two Venn diagrams
    grid.newpage()
    pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(2, 1)))
    # Add the positive diagram to the top
    pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1))
    grid.draw(pos_venn)
    popViewport()
    # Add the negative diagram to the bottom
    pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 1))
    grid.draw(neg_venn)
    popViewport(2)
    dev.off()
    
    # Create a simple text summary
    summary_file <- gsub(".pdf$", "_summary.txt", output_file)
    sink(summary_file)
    cat(paste("Detailed direction Venn diagrams for", table1, "vs", table2), "\n\n")
    cat("SIGNIFICANCE CRITERIA:\n")
    cat("- POSITIVE: coef > log2(1.25) & FDR < 0.1\n")
    cat("- NEGATIVE: coef < log2(0.75) & FDR < 0.1\n\n")
    
    cat("POSITIVE ELEMENTS:\n")
    cat(paste("Positive in", table1, "only:", length(pos_in_table1_only)), "\n")
    cat(paste("Positive in", table2, "only:", length(pos_in_table2_only)), "\n")
    cat(paste("Positive in both:", length(pos_in_both)), "\n\n")
    
    cat("NEGATIVE ELEMENTS:\n")
    cat(paste("Negative in", table1, "only:", length(neg_in_table1_only)), "\n")
    cat(paste("Negative in", table2, "only:", length(neg_in_table2_only)), "\n")
    cat(paste("Negative in both:", length(neg_in_both)), "\n\n")
    
    cat("OPPOSITE DIRECTION ELEMENTS (excluded from main Venn):\n")
    cat(paste("Positive in", table1, "but Negative in", table2, ":", 
              length(intersect(table1_pos, table2_neg))), "\n")
    cat(paste("Negative in", table1, "but Positive in", table2, ":", 
              length(intersect(table1_neg, table2_pos))), "\n")
    sink()
  }
  
  return(TRUE)
}

run_pairwise_comparisons<-function() {
  # Use the existing data tables instead of creating mock data
  # Assumes 'intron', 'exon', and 'empra' are already loaded in your R environment
  
  # Create the data list with the correct table names
  data_list <- list(
    shuf_presplice = shuf_presplice,
    shuf_postsplice = shuf_postsplice,
    shuf_empra = shuf_empra
  )
  
  # Process the data with custom thresholds
  # Positive: logFC > log2(1.25) & FDR < 0.1
  # Negative: logFC < log2(0.75) & FDR < 0.1
  processed_data <- process_tables(
    data_list, 
    fdr_threshold = 0.1, 
    pos_fold_change = log2(1.25), 
    neg_fold_change = log2(0.75)
  )
  
  # Define output directory
  output_dir <- "venn_diagrams_results_shuffled_updatedmethod/"
  dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  
  # Define the specific comparisons you want with the new table names
  comparisons <- list(
    c("shuf_presplice", "shuf_empra"),
    c("shuf_postsplice", "shuf_empra"),
    c("shuf_presplice", "shuf_postsplice")
  )
  
  # Run each comparison
  for (comp in comparisons) {
    table1 <- comp[1]
    table2 <- comp[2]
    
    # Create main Venn diagram
    create_direction_venn(
      processed_data, 
      table1, 
      table2, 
      output_file = paste0(output_dir, table1, "_vs_", table2, "_venn.pdf")
    )
    
    # Create detailed direction Venn
    create_detailed_direction_venn(
      processed_data, 
      table1, 
      table2, 
      output_file = paste0(output_dir, table1, "_vs_", table2, "_detailed.pdf")
    )
  }
  
  cat("\nVenn diagrams and summary files have been created in the", output_dir, "directory\n")
}
```

# Part 1 — Sequencing QC and count assembly

This part reproduces the 5/23/25 re-analysis: it reads the raw per-sample count
tables, runs alignment and replicate-correlation QC, and reshapes the data into
the long 'UTR' format. The final two chunks write
`invivo.ps1.utr.format.5.23.25.rds` and `empratrev.utr.format.5.23.25.rds`, which
Part 2 reads back in.

## ISO-MPRA count tables

Read every `ms*.txt` ISO-MPRA count table, standardize the element IDs, sum the
technical re-sequencing runs into one post-splice count per sample, and merge all
samples into the wide `merged_data` table keyed by `rsID`.

```{r p1-assemble-isompra-counts, include=FALSE}
#The following is now going to bring in the ISOMPRA format files which are already in a table as the bash script aligns and then counts for us.
files <- list.files(pattern = "ms.*.txt")
files <- files[!grepl("foundBCS\\.txt",files)]
# Loop through each file
for (file in files) {
  # Read the data from the file (adjust read.table parameters as needed)
  data <- fread(file, header = TRUE, fill = TRUE)
  # Apply the specified transformations to the 'ID' column
  data$ID <- sub(".*\\|", "", data$ID)
  data$ID <- ifelse(grepl("^ X", data$ID), paste0("trevino.ctrl", data$ID), data$ID)
  data$ID <- sub("trevino.ctrl\\s*X", "trevino.ctrlX", data$ID)
  data$ID <- gsub("\\s+", "", data$ID)
  data$ID <- as.character(data$ID)
  data$ID <- ifelse(grepl("rs\\d+", data$ID) & !grepl("=", data$ID),
                    paste0("scrambled", data$ID), data$ID)
  # Save the modified data to the environment with a unique name
  assign(paste0("modified_", tools::file_path_sans_ext(file)), data)
}
```

## eMPRA barcode count tables

Read the per-sample found-barcode lists, reverse-complement to library orientation,
associate each barcode with its element via `trevino.names.csv`, and sum technical
runs into `SIC_countstrevino` (wide, barcode-level).

```{r p1-assemble-empra-counts, include=FALSE}
#These lines of code read in the found BCs and then rev comp them to match the library so we can associate the BC with the correct Element
SIC_countstrevino<-fread("trevino.names.csv",header=F,fill=T)
colnames(SIC_countstrevino)<-c("revcomp_barcode","rsID")
SIC_countstrevino$revcomp_barcode<- sapply(SIC_countstrevino$revcomp_barcode, function(x) as.character(reverseComplement(DNAString(x))))
bcfinds <- list.files(pattern='BCS.txt',full.names = TRUE)
i<-1
for (i in c(1:length(bcfinds))){  
  curfinds <- fread(paste0(bcfinds[i]),header=FALSE)  
  curcounts <- as.data.table(table(curfinds))  
  setnames(curcounts,c(1:2),c("revcomp_barcode", gsub(bcfinds[i],pattern="^(.*)_foundBCs.txt",replacement="\\1")))  
  SIC_countstrevino <- merge.data.table(curcounts,SIC_countstrevino,by="revcomp_barcode",all.y=TRUE)
}

rm(curcounts,curfinds)
```

## ISO-MPRA percent alignment

Per-sample reads aligned, percent aligned, and fraction of the 466 library elements
detected.

```{r p1-qc-percent-alignment-isompra, include=TRUE}
trevino.meta.file<-read_csv("trevino.names.csv",col_names=F)

trevino.meta.file<-trevino.meta.file[,c(2)]
trevino.meta.file<-distinct(trevino.meta.file)
names(trevino.meta.file)<-c("rsID")
trevino<-merged_data
trevino[trevino == 0] <- NA
trevino<-inner_join(trevino.meta.file,trevino,by="rsID")

mappedcounts<-as.data.table(colSums(trevino[,c(2:38)],na.rm=T),keep.rownames=T)
names(mappedcounts)<-c("sample","V2")
totalreadsout<-merge.data.table(totalreads,mappedcounts,by="sample")

setnames(totalreadsout,3,"reads_aligned")
totalreadsout[,pctalign:=(reads_aligned/counts)*100]

i<-0
for (i in c(0:nrow(totalreadsout))){  
  cursample <- names(trevino)[i+1]  
  counted <- sum(!is.na(trevino[,(i+1),with=FALSE])) 
  totalreadsout[sample==cursample, BCs_counted:=counted]
  totalreadsout[sample == cursample, pctElems_Counted := counted / 466 * 100]
}

totalreadsout.trevino.isompra<-totalreadsout
print(totalreadsout.trevino.isompra)
write.csv(totalreadsout.trevino.isompra,"reads.table.trevino.isompra.csv")

rm(mappedcounts,totalreadsout)
```

## eMPRA percent alignment

The same QC metrics for the eMPRA samples (denominator ~9,400 barcodes).

```{r p1-qc-percent-alignment-empra, include=TRUE}
mappedcounts<-as.data.table(colSums(SIC_countstrevino[,c(2:25)],na.rm=T),keep.rownames=T)
names(mappedcounts)<-c("sample","V2")
totalreadsout<-merge.data.table(totalreads.empra,mappedcounts,by="sample")

setnames(totalreadsout,3,"reads_aligned")
totalreadsout[,pctalign:=(reads_aligned/counts)*100]

i<-1
for (i in c(1:nrow(totalreadsout))){  
  cursample <- names(SIC_countstrevino)[i+1]  
  counted <- sum(!is.na(SIC_countstrevino[,(i+1),with=FALSE]))  
  totalreadsout[sample==cursample, BCs_counted:=counted]
  totalreadsout[sample == cursample, pctBCs_Counted := counted / 9400 * 100]
}

totalreadsout.trevino<-totalreadsout
print(totalreadsout.trevino)
write.csv(totalreadsout.trevino,"reads.table.trevino.empra.csv")
```

## Combined QC plots

Combine the ISO-MPRA and eMPRA QC tables into long form and plot reads aligned,
percent aligned, and percent counted across replicates and methods.

```{r p1-qc-plots, include=TRUE}
# Copy and rename for consistency
trevino1 <- copy(totalreadsout.trevino.isompra)[, `:=`(
  Source = "ISOMPRA",
  Condition = fifelse(grepl("pre", sample), "Pre", 
                      fifelse(grepl("post", sample), "Post", "Pre")),
  pct_counted = pctElems_Counted
)]

trevino2 <- copy(totalreadsout.trevino)[, `:=`(
  Source = "eMPRA",
  Condition = "All",
  pct_counted = pctBCs_Counted
)]

#trevino3 <- copy(totalreadsout.trevino.14)[, `:=`(
  #Source = "eMPRA.down",
 # Condition = "All",
  #pct_counted = pctBCs_Counted
#)]

# Combine them into one long-form table
combined <- rbindlist(list(trevino1, trevino2), fill = TRUE)

long_combined <- melt(
  rbindlist(list(trevino1, trevino2), fill = TRUE),
  id.vars = c("sample", "Source", "Condition"),
  measure.vars = c("reads_aligned", "pctalign", "pct_counted"),
  variable.name = "Metric",
  value.name = "Value"
)

# Boxplot with points for each replicate
ggplot(long_combined, aes(x = interaction(Source, Condition), y = Value, fill = Source)) +
     geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
     geom_jitter(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
     facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
     labs(
         title = "Metrics Across Replicates and Methods",
         x = "Method + Condition",
         y = "Value"
     ) +
     scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8e3636", "#E1BE6A", "#E1BE6A")) +
     theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
     theme(
         legend.position = "bottom",
         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
         strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
         strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
         panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
     )
```

## Raw-count expression comparison (eMPRA vs ISO-MPRA)

Filter each dataset by minimum unique-barcode thresholds, compute log2(RNA/DNA)
expression, and correlate eMPRA against pre- and post-spliced ISO-MPRA expression
at several thresholds; also build per-replicate and barcode-vs-element correlation
summaries.

```{r p1-raw-expression-comparison, include=TRUE}
trevino.old<-trevino
#-------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Load and Clean Input Data
#-------------------------------------------------------
cols_to_rename <- !grepl("\\.post$", colnames(trevino)) & 
                  !grepl("rsID", colnames(trevino)) & 
                  !grepl("aav",colnames(trevino))&
                  !grepl("plasmid",colnames(trevino))&
                  colnames(trevino) != "revcomp_barcode"
colnames(trevino)[cols_to_rename] <- paste0(colnames(trevino)[cols_to_rename], ".pre")

data.empra <- SIC_countstrevino
tmp<-SIC_countstrevino[,c(1,26)]
tmp<-tmp %>% distinct(rsID, .keep_all = TRUE)
data.isompra<-full_join(trevino,tmp,by="rsID")


# Remove NA rows
data.empra <- data.empra[rowSums(is.na(data.empra[,2:25])) == 0, ]
data.isompra <- data.isompra[rowSums(is.na(data.isompra[,2:38])) == 0, ]

# Create the 4 data.tables with different thresholds
dt_1plus<-create_filtered_table(data.empra,1)
dt_5plus <- create_filtered_table(data.empra, 5)
dt_10plus <- create_filtered_table(data.empra, 10)
dt_15plus <- create_filtered_table(data.empra, 15)
dt_20plus <- create_filtered_table(data.empra, 20)

#----------------------------------------
# For data.empra filtered tables
#----------------------------------------

# Calculate expression for empra tables using dna1
expr_dt_1plus <-calculate_expression(dt_1plus,"aav")
expr_dt_5plus <- calculate_expression(dt_5plus, "aav")
expr_dt_10plus <- calculate_expression(dt_10plus, "aav")
expr_dt_15plus <- calculate_expression(dt_15plus, "aav")
expr_dt_20plus <- calculate_expression(dt_20plus, "aav")

#----------------------------------------
# For data.isompra filtered tables
#----------------------------------------
#---------- Main analysis ----------#

# 1. Split data.isompra into pre-spliced and post-spliced
isompra_split <- split_isompra_data(data.isompra)
pre_splice_dt <- isompra_split$pre_splice
post_splice_dt <- isompra_split$post_splice
pre_splice_cols <- isompra_split$pre_cols
post_splice_cols <- isompra_split$post_cols

# 2. Calculate expression for pre-spliced and post-spliced data
pre_splice_expr <- calculate_expression(pre_splice_dt, "aav")
post_splice_expr <- calculate_expression(post_splice_dt, "aav")

# 3. Calculate average expression across replicates
pre_splice_avg <- calculate_average_expression(pre_splice_expr$expr_dt, pre_splice_expr$expr_cols)
post_splice_avg <- calculate_average_expression(post_splice_expr$expr_dt, post_splice_expr$expr_cols)

#-------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Run Main EMPRA vs ISOMPRA Pipeline
#-------------------------------------------------------
results_standard <- process_empra_vs_isompra(SIC_countstrevino, trevino, prefix = "standard")


all_results <- c(results_standard)
all_summaries <- rbindlist(lapply(all_results, function(x) x$summary))
all_plots <- lapply(all_results, function(x) x$plot)

# Create and save grid of scatter plots
correlation_grid <- do.call(grid.arrange, c(all_plots, ncol = 2))
ggsave("correlation_grid_all.png", correlation_grid, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = 300)

# Melt and plot barplot of correlation summary
summary_long <- melt(all_summaries,
                     id.vars = c("threshold", "splice_type", "n_rsids"),
                     measure.vars = c("pearson_cor", "spearman_cor"),
                     variable.name = "correlation_type",
                     value.name = "correlation")
summary_long$correlation_type <- ifelse(summary_long$correlation_type == "pearson_cor", "Pearson", "Spearman")

correlation_barplot <- ggplot(summary_long,
                              aes(x = factor(threshold), y = correlation,
                                  fill = interaction(splice_type, correlation_type))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", correlation)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Between eMPRA and ISOMPRA Expression",
       x = "Minimum Unique Barcodes Threshold",
       y = "Correlation Coefficient",
       fill = "Data Type") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

ggsave("correlation_barplot_all.png", correlation_barplot, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

#-------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Intra-Dataset Correlograms (standard + down)
#-------------------------------------------------------

# --- eMPRA Standard ---
empra_expr_dt_name <- "expr_dt_1plus"
empra_expr_raw <- get(empra_expr_dt_name)

empra_input <- if (is.list(empra_expr_raw) && !is.data.frame(empra_expr_raw) && "expr_dt" %in% names(empra_expr_raw)) {
  empra_expr_raw
} else {
  list(expr_dt = empra_expr_raw, expr_cols = grep("^expr_", names(empra_expr_raw), value = TRUE))
}

empra_pearson <- create_correlogram(empra_input, "eMPRA Replicates Correlation", method = "pearson")
empra_spearman <- create_correlogram(empra_input, "eMPRA Replicates Correlation", method = "spearman")
empra_pearson_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(empra_pearson)
empra_spearman_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(empra_spearman)
empra_pearson_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(empra_pearson)
empra_spearman_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(empra_spearman)

# --- Pre-Splice Standard ---
pre_input <- list(expr_dt = pre_splice_expr$expr_dt,
                  expr_cols = grep("^expr_", names(pre_splice_expr$expr_dt), value = TRUE))

pre_pearson <- create_correlogram(pre_input, "Pre-Splice Replicates Correlation", method = "pearson")
pre_spearman <- create_correlogram(pre_input, "Pre-Splice Replicates Correlation", method = "spearman")
pre_pearson_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(pre_pearson)
pre_spearman_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(pre_spearman)
pre_pearson_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(pre_pearson)
pre_spearman_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(pre_spearman)

# --- Post-Splice Standard ---
post_input <- list(expr_dt = post_splice_expr$expr_dt,
                   expr_cols = grep("^expr_", names(post_splice_expr$expr_dt), value = TRUE))

post_pearson <- create_correlogram(post_input, "Post-Splice Replicates Correlation", method = "pearson")
post_spearman <- create_correlogram(post_input, "Post-Splice Replicates Correlation", method = "spearman")
post_pearson_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(post_pearson)
post_spearman_avg <- calculate_avg_correlation(post_spearman)
post_pearson_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(post_pearson)
post_spearman_avg_reps<-calculate_avg_correlation_per_replicate(post_spearman)

#-------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Pre vs Post-Splice Comparison
#-------------------------------------------------------
pre_post_comparison <- merge(pre_splice_avg, post_splice_avg, by = "rsID", suffixes = c("_pre", "_post"))

pre_post_pearson <- cor.test(pre_post_comparison$avg_expr_pre,
                             pre_post_comparison$avg_expr_post,
                             method = "pearson")

pre_post_spearman <- cor.test(pre_post_comparison$avg_expr_pre,
                              pre_post_comparison$avg_expr_post,
                              method = "spearman")

pre_post_plot <- ggplot(pre_post_comparison, aes(x = avg_expr_pre, y = avg_expr_post)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Pre-Splice vs Post-Splice Expression Correlation",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Pearson r = ", round(pre_post_pearson$estimate, 3),
      " (p = ", format.pval(pre_post_pearson$p.value, digits = 3), ")\n",
      "Spearman ρ = ", round(pre_post_spearman$estimate, 3),
      " (p = ", format.pval(pre_post_spearman$p.value, digits = 3), ")"
    ),
    x = "Pre-Splice Average Expression",
    y = "Post-Splice Average Expression"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

ggsave("correlogram_plots/pre_vs_post_splice.png", pre_post_plot, width = 8, height = 6)

#-------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Summary Tables & Plot
#-------------------------------------------------------
replicate_corr_summary <- data.table(
  data_type = c("eMPRA", "eMPRA", "Pre-Splice", "Pre-Splice", "Post-Splice", "Post-Splice"),
  method = c("Pearson", "Spearman", "Pearson", "Spearman", "Pearson", "Spearman"),
  mean_correlation = c(empra_pearson_avg$mean, empra_spearman_avg$mean,
                       pre_pearson_avg$mean, pre_spearman_avg$mean,
                       post_pearson_avg$mean, post_spearman_avg$mean),
  median_correlation = c(empra_pearson_avg$median, empra_spearman_avg$median,
                         pre_pearson_avg$median, pre_spearman_avg$median,
                         post_pearson_avg$median, post_spearman_avg$median),
  min_correlation = c(empra_pearson_avg$min, empra_spearman_avg$min,
                      pre_pearson_avg$min, pre_spearman_avg$min,
                      post_pearson_avg$min, post_spearman_avg$min),
  max_correlation = c(empra_pearson_avg$max, empra_spearman_avg$max,
                      pre_pearson_avg$max, pre_spearman_avg$max,
                      post_pearson_avg$max, post_spearman_avg$max)
)

pre_post_summary <- data.table(
  comparison = c("Pre-Splice vs Post-Splice", "Pre-Splice vs Post-Splice"),
  method = c("Pearson", "Spearman"),
  correlation = c(pre_post_pearson$estimate, pre_post_spearman$estimate),
  p_value = c(pre_post_pearson$p.value, pre_post_spearman$p.value)
)

print("Intra-Replicate Correlation Summary:")
print(replicate_corr_summary)

print("Pre-Splice vs Post-Splice Correlation:")
print(pre_post_summary)

# Barplot of intra-replicate mean correlations
ggplot(replicate_corr_summary, aes(x = data_type, y = mean_correlation, fill = method)) +
```

## CPM-based correlations

Repeat the replicate-correlation analysis on the CPM scale rather than raw counts.

```{r p1-cpm-correlation, include=TRUE}
calculate_cpm <- function(dt, dna_col) {
  expr_cols <- grep("^ms|^rna", colnames(dt), value = TRUE)
  cpm_values <- dt[, (expr_cols) := lapply(.SD, function(x) (x / sum(x)) * 1e6), .SDcols = expr_cols]
  # Rename columns with "cpm_" prefix
  setnames(dt, expr_cols, paste0("cpm_", expr_cols))
  return(list(expr_dt = dt, expr_cols = paste0("cpm_", expr_cols)))
}

# Helper function to calculate average pairwise Spearman correlation among replicates
get_avg_spearman <-function(dt, data_type) {
  # Get numeric columns only
  numeric_cols <- names(dt)[sapply(dt, is.numeric)]
  
  # Extract numeric data
  numeric_data <- as.matrix(dt[, ..numeric_cols])
  
  # Check for sufficient columns
  if (ncol(numeric_data) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(correlation = NA, replicate1 = NA, replicate2 = NA, data_type = data_type))
  }
  
  # Compute correlation matrix
  corr_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  
  # Get upper triangle indices
  upper_tri_indices <- which(upper.tri(corr_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
  
  # Extract values and replicate names
  replicate1 <- colnames(corr_matrix)[upper_tri_indices[, 1]]
  replicate2 <- colnames(corr_matrix)[upper_tri_indices[, 2]]
  correlation <- corr_matrix[upper_tri_indices]
  
  # Return as data.frame
  data.frame(
    replicate1 = replicate1,
    replicate2 = replicate2,
    correlation = correlation,
    data_type = data_type
  )
}

# Compute for each data.table
spearman_empra <- get_avg_spearman(data.empra, "data.empra")
spearman_pre <- get_avg_spearman(pre_splice_dt, "presplice")
spearman_post <- get_avg_spearman(post_splice_dt, "postsplice")

# Combine all

  spearman_empra,
  spearman_pre,
  spearman_post
)

  measure.vars = c("replicate1", "replicate2"),
  value.name = "replicate"
)

# Convert to data.table for group operations

  avg_correlation = mean(correlation, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(data_type, replicate)]

  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.7) +
```

```{r p1-correlations-empra, include=TRUE}
pairs.panels(tmp[,c(41:57)], 
             method = "spearman", # correlation method
             hist.col = "seagreen",
             density = TRUE,  # show density plots
             ellipses = TRUE,
             lm=T,
             pch="."# show correlation ellipses
             )

cor_matrix <- cor(tmp[,c(41:57)], use = "pairwise.complete.obs",method="spearman")

# Convert to a data frame
cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_matrix)

# Save as CSV
write.csv(cor_df, file = "corr.empra.trevino.expr.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```

# Part 2 — Downstream MPRA analysis

Part 2 begins by reading back the long-format `.rds` files written at the end of
Part 1, normalizing them (edgeR) and computing per-element expression. It then
runs the full set of downstream analyses: barcode-count summaries, replicate and
cross-comparison correlation plots, enhancer/repressor and allelic-effect linear
(mixed) models, direction/overlap Venn diagrams, GC-content vs expression checks,
and burden testing. Section dividers from the original notebook are preserved as
headings below.

## Pre, Post and Total Expression Tables

```{r Importing Data, include = T}

data.isompra <- readRDS("invivo.ps1.utr.format.5.23.25.rds")
data.empra <- readRDS("empratrev.utr.format.5.23.25.rds")

data.isompra$sex <- ifelse(grepl("dna.total", data.isompra$Fraction), 'DNA', 
                         ifelse(data.isompra$BiolRep %in% c("3","5","6","7","11","12","20","22","23","27","28"), 'Male', 'Female'))

data.empra$sex <- ifelse(grepl("dna.total", data.empra$Fraction), 'DNA', 
                         ifelse(data.empra$BiolRep %in% c("2","4","8","14","16","17"), 'Female', 'Male'))

data.isompra$SpliceStatus <- ifelse(grepl("dna.total", data.isompra$Fraction), 'DNA', 
                         ifelse(data.isompra$BiolRep %in% c(1:17), 'Pre', 'Post'))

presplice <- filter(data.isompra, SpliceStatus %in% c("Pre", "DNA"))
postsplice <- filter(data.isompra, SpliceStatus %in% c("Post", "DNA"))

presplice <- aggregate.counts(data=presplice,
                      by.field="Fraction",
                      agg.level="dna.total",
                      new.level="dna.agg",
                      rep.fields="BiolRep",
                      new.rep.levels = 1,
                      sample.fields = c("Fraction","BiolRep"))

postsplice <- aggregate.counts(data=postsplice,
                      by.field="Fraction",
                      agg.level="dna.total",
                      new.level="dna.agg",
                      rep.fields="BiolRep",
                      new.rep.levels = 1,
                      sample.fields = c("Fraction","BiolRep"))

data.empra<-aggregate.counts(data=data.empra,
                      by.field="Fraction",
                      agg.level="dna.total",
                      new.level="dna.agg",
                      rep.fields="BiolRep",
                      new.rep.levels = 1,
                      sample.fields = c("Fraction","BiolRep"))

#EdgeR Normalization
presplice<-normalize.counts.edgeR(presplice,sample.fields=c("Experiment","Fraction","BiolRep","TechRep"),element.fields = c("Element","Allele"))
postsplice<-normalize.counts.edgeR(postsplice,sample.fields=c("Experiment","Fraction","BiolRep","TechRep"),element.fields = c("Element","Allele"))
data.empra<-normalize.counts.edgeR(data.empra,sample.fields=c("Experiment","Fraction","BiolRep","TechRep"),element.fields = c("Element","Allele","BC","revcomp_barcode"))

#Computing Expression
presplice<-compute.expression(data=presplice,
                            steps = list(c('normalize','Fraction', 'rna.total',
                                           'dna.agg', 'BiolRep'),
                                         c('log'))) 

postsplice<-compute.expression(data=postsplice,
                            steps = list(c('normalize','Fraction', 'rna.total',
                                           'dna.agg', 'BiolRep'),
                                         c('log'))) 

data.empra <- compute.expression(data=data.empra,
                            steps = list(c('normalize','Fraction', 'rna.total',
                                           'dna.agg', 'BiolRep'),
                                         c('log')))


presplice$BC <- paste0(presplice$Allele,presplice$BC)
presplice[, Element := lapply(Element, extract_and_replace)]
presplice$Element <- str_replace_all(presplice$Element,"=.*$","")
cols <- c("BiolRep","Element","TechRep","Allele","BC")
set(presplice, j = cols, value = lapply(presplice[, ..cols], as.factor))

postsplice$BC <- paste0(postsplice$Allele,postsplice$BC)
postsplice[, Element := lapply(Element, extract_and_replace)]
postsplice$Element <- str_replace_all(postsplice$Element,"=.*$","")
cols <- c("BiolRep","Element","TechRep","Allele","BC")
set(postsplice, j = cols, value = lapply(postsplice[, ..cols], as.factor))

data.empra$BC <- paste0(data.empra$Allele,data.empra$BC)
data.empra[, Element := lapply(Element, extract_and_replace)]
data.empra$Element <- str_replace_all(data.empra$Element,"=.*$","")
cols <- c("BiolRep","Element","TechRep","Allele","BC")
set(data.empra, j = cols, value = lapply(data.empra[, ..cols], as.factor))

data.isompra<-bind_rows(presplice,postsplice)


```

```{r Counting Number of Barcodes eMPRA, include=T}

data.empra.bc<-data.empra
data.empra.bc[, BCType := fifelse(grepl("alt", BC, ignore.case = TRUE), "alt",
                       fifelse(grepl("ref", BC, ignore.case = TRUE), "ref", "other"))]

# Count unique instances of BC per Element, BiolRep, and BC type
barcodes <- data.empra.bc[, .(UniqueBCCount = uniqueN(BC)), by = .(Element, BiolRep, BCType)]

barcodes.avg<-barcodes[, .(AvgUniqueBCCount = mean(UniqueBCCount)), by = .(Element, BCType)]

count_below_thresholds <- barcodes.avg[, .(
  Above1 = sum(AvgUniqueBCCount>1),
  Above5 = sum(AvgUniqueBCCount > 5),
  Above10 = sum(AvgUniqueBCCount > 10),
  Above15 = sum(AvgUniqueBCCount > 15),
  Equal20 = sum(AvgUniqueBCCount >= 20)
)]

print(count_below_thresholds)

count_thresholds_long <- melt(count_below_thresholds, variable.name = "Threshold", value.name = "Count")

ggplot(count_thresholds_long, aes(x = Threshold, y = Count, fill = Threshold)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8e3636","#8e3636","#a84c4c", "#c06262", "#d97878","#f2b1b1")) +
  labs(title = "Count of Elements Below Thresholds", x = "Threshold", y = "Number of Elements") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave("counts_by_bc_filtered_over20_counts.png", width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r Comparison Graphs Element, include = T}
# Example usage:
result_table <- filter_with_allele_counts(data.empra.bc)

avg_expression_table_over_5 <- calculate_expression_stats(filtered_over_5)

postsplice_element_avg <- calculate_element_avg_expression(postsplice)

# First, put all your datasets in a list
data_list <- list(
  presplice_element_avg,

# View the results
```
